title: An analysis of the three-dimensional kinetics and kinematics of maximal effort punches among amateur boxers
journal_or_venue: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport
retraction_or_correction_status: no retraction or correction recorded in OpenAlex at accessed_at
notes: cited_by_count 57 at harvest; a citation count is a measure of attention, not of correctness
methodology: 3D motion capture of the upper body plus two force plates under lead and rear legs; maximal-effort punches into a suspended bag; six punch types compared.
study_population: amateur male boxers, mean 6.3 years experience
main_findings: Straight, hook and uppercut differ significantly on every measured variable except elbow angular velocity - the three families are not the same action at different speeds.
The lead hook carried the highest peak fist velocity and the jab the shortest delivery time, so speed of hand and speed of arrival are different quantities.
Ground reaction force differed significantly between rear and lead legs for the jab only, which places the legs inside the punch rather than under it.
limitations: bag work at maximal effort, not an opponent under exchange
descriptive, so it ranks punches without predicting outcome

quoted_evidence.quote: The lead hook exhibited the greatest peak fist velocity (11.95 m/s), the jab the shortest delivery time (405 ms)

project_implications: Supports the move table treating startup and delivery separately from reach and force rather than deriving one from the other.

A question for the animation model, not an answer: if the jab is the fastest to arrive but not the fastest hand, our startup frames and our tip-extension ramp are describing two different real quantities and should not be tuned as one.
